name: Feminist separatism
summary: Feminist separatism holds that women should withdraw, in many forms and degrees, from men and from male-defined institutions and relationships, and build their own groups, meetings and projects. Its main philosophical statement, Marilyn Frye's 1977 paper, treats excluding men as an assumption of power through control of access, and ties separation to lesbian life, leaving marriage and divorcing, and abortion. It is a strategy and a way of reading male power more than a full political programme, so it speaks little on economics, government or world affairs.
scope: The voluntary, women-initiated separatism of 1970s lesbian-feminist writing, represented by Frye's "Some Reflections on Separatism and Power" (Sinister Wisdom 6, 1978) and by Susan Krieger's advocacy of separate women's organisations in The Family Silver (1996), with the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy article on feminist power for context. It excludes masculist segregation imposed by men, the positions of feminism as a family, lesbian feminism as a whole, and any single separatist's views on topics Frye and Krieger do not address.
